text: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed set of nodes (the reservoir) that are randomly connected and have their weights set during training. The weights of the output layer are then trained to map the reservoir's activations to the desired output. Training typically involves a simple linear regression on the reservoir's activations to learn the output weights, making the training process fast and efficient. Reservoirs in ESNs are usually trained using random weights, focusing on capturing the dynamics of the input data rather than learning specific tasks.
